title.en: Volume 301 Biographies 60: Bian Su, Mei Xun, Ma Yuanfang, Xue Tian, Kou Jian, Yang Riyan, Li Xingjian, Zhang Pin, Chen Yan, Li You, Zhang Bing, Zhang Zhaixing, Zheng Xiang, Guo Zhen, Zhao He, Gao Di, Yuan Kang, Xu Qi, Zhang Zhi, Qi Kuo, Zheng Xiang
title.raw: 卷三百〇一 列傳第六十 邊肅 梅詢 馬元方 薛田 寇瑊 楊日嚴 李行簡 章頻 陳琰 李宥 張秉 張擇行 鄭向 郭稹 趙賀 高覿 袁抗 徐起 張旨 齊廓 鄭驤 Volume 301 Biographies 60: Bian Su, Mei Xun, Ma Yuanfang, Xue Tian, Kou Jian, Yang Riyan, Li Xingjian, Zhang Pin, Chen Yan, Li You, Zhang Bing, Zhang Zhaixing, Zheng Xiang, Guo Zhen, Zhao He, Gao Di, Yuan Kang, Xu Qi, Zhang Zhi, Qi Kuo, Zheng Xiang

sentences.zh: 邊肅，字安國，應天府楚丘人。

translations.literal: Bian Su, courtesy name Anguo, was a man of Chuqiu in Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Su, styled Anguo, was a native of Chuqiu in Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 進士及第，除大理評事、知於潛縣，累遷太常博士。

translations.literal: Having passed the jinshi examination, he was appointed Dali pingshi and prefect of Yuqian County, and was promoted in succession to Taichang boshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review and magistrate of Yuqian County, rising in due course to erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 三司使魏羽薦為戶部判官，祀南郊，超薦尚書度支員外郎。

translations.literal: The Three Departments commissioner Wei Yu recommended him as Hubu pangguan; when sacrificing to the southern suburbs, he was extraordinarily promoted to Shangshu duzhi yuanwailang.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Yu served as commissioner of the Three Departments, he recommended Su as an aide in the Ministry of Revenue; on the southern suburbs sacrifice, Su received an exceptional promotion to vice director in the Bureau of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 帝以三司鉤取無法，至道初，置行帳司，以會財用之數，命肅主之。

translations.literal: The emperor, because the Three Departments' audits had no proper method, in the early Zhidao era established a traveling-accounts office to reconcile fiscal accounts and ordered Su to head it.
translations.idiomatic: Because the emperor believed the Three Departments' audits lacked proper method, in the early Zhidao era a traveling-accounts office was established to reconcile fiscal accounts, and Su was ordered to head it.

sentences.zh: 帳成，遷工部郎中。

translations.literal: When the account was completed, he was transferred to langzhong in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When the account was completed, he was promoted to director in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 真宗幸大名府，命肅經度行在糧草。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhenzong visited Daming Prefecture, he ordered Su to manage provisions for the traveling court.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhenzong visited Daming Prefecture, Su was ordered to manage provisions for the traveling court.

sentences.zh: 改判開拆司，出知曹州，徙邢州。

translations.literal: He was changed to judge the Disbursement Office, sent out as prefect of Cao Prefecture, and transferred to Xing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned to judge the Disbursement Office, then sent out as prefect of Cao Prefecture and transferred to Xing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 會契丹大入，先是地屢震，城堞摧圮，無守備，帝在澶州，密詔肅：「若州不可守，聽便宜南保他城。

translations.literal: It happened that the Khitan invaded on a large scale; beforehand the ground had repeatedly trembled, city walls and parapets had collapsed, and there was no defense—the emperor at Chanyuan secretly instructed Su: "If the prefecture cannot be held, you may at discretion withdraw south and preserve another city."
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan invaded on a large scale, the ground in the region had repeatedly trembled beforehand, city walls and parapets had collapsed, and there was no defense—the emperor at Chanyuan secretly told Su: "If the prefecture cannot be held, you may at discretion withdraw south and preserve another city."

sentences.zh: 」肅匿詔不發，督丁壯乘城而辟諸門，悉所部兵陣以代之。

translations.literal: Su kept the edict sealed and did not publish it; he pressed the able-bodied to man the walls and opened all the gates, posting his entire command in formation in place of the regular garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Su kept the edict sealed and did not publish it; he pressed the able-bodied to man the walls and opened all the gates, posting his entire command in formation in place of the regular garrison.

sentences.zh: 騎傅城下，肅與戰小勝，契丹莫測也，居三日，引去。

translations.literal: Cavalry pressed the walls; Su fought them and gained a small victory. The Khitan could not fathom his strength and, after three days, withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Cavalry pressed the walls; Su fought them and gained a small victory. The Khitan could not fathom his strength and, after three days, withdrew.

sentences.zh: 時鎮、魏、深、趙、磁、洺六州閉壁不出，老幼趨城者，肅悉開門納之。

translations.literal: At the time the six prefectures of Zhen, Wei, Shen, Zhao, Ci, and Luo shut their walls and would not come out; Su opened the gates and admitted all the old and young who fled toward the city.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the six prefectures of Zhen, Wei, Shen, Zhao, Ci, and Luo shut their walls and would not come out; Su opened the gates and admitted all the old and young who fled toward the city.

sentences.zh: 擢樞密直學士，徙宣州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to academician in the Palace Secretariat and transferred to Xuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to academician in the Palace Secretariat and transferred to Xuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 車駕朝陵，徙河南府。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage went to pay respects at the tombs, he was moved to Henan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage went to pay respects at the tombs, he was moved to Henan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 還，勾當三班院。

translations.literal: On his return he supervised the Three-Rank Court.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he supervised the Three-Rank Court.

sentences.zh: 出知天雄軍，徙真定府，累遷給事中。

translations.literal: He was sent out as military commissioner of Tianxiong Army, moved to Zhending Prefecture, and was promoted in succession to supervisory censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as military commissioner of Tianxiong Army, then moved to Zhending Prefecture, and was promoted in succession to supervisory censor.

sentences.zh: 以王嗣宗代肅。

translations.literal: Wang Sizong replaced Su.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sizong replaced Su.

sentences.zh: 嗣宗與肅有舊隙，諷通判東方慶訟肅前在州，私以公錢貿易規利，遣吏強市民羊，買女口自入。

translations.literal: Sizong and Su had an old enmity; Sizong instigated the vice prefect Dong Fangqing to sue Su for his earlier tenure in the prefecture—privately using public funds for trading to seek profit, sending officers to coerce citizens' sheep, and buying women for his own household.
translations.idiomatic: Sizong and Su had an old enmity; Sizong instigated the vice prefect Dong Fangqing to sue Su for his earlier tenure in the prefecture—privately using public funds for trading to seek profit, sending officers to coerce citizens' sheep, and buying women for his own household.

sentences.zh: 嗣宗上其事，帝以肅近臣，不欲屬吏，遣劉綜、任中正以章示之，肅引伏。

translations.literal: Sizong memorialized these matters; because Su was a close minister the emperor did not want to hand him to judicial officials but sent Liu Zong and Ren Zhongzheng to show him the charges, and Su confessed.
translations.idiomatic: Sizong memorialized these matters; because Su was a close minister the emperor did not want to hand him to judicial officials but sent Liu Zong and Ren Zhongzheng to show him the charges, and Su confessed.

sentences.zh: 以守城功，止奪三官，貶岳州團練副使。

translations.literal: In consideration of his merit in defending the city, only three ranks were stripped from him and he was demoted to deputy military training commissioner of Yue Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In consideration of his merit in defending the city, only three ranks were stripped from him and he was demoted to deputy military training commissioner of Yue Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 久之，徙武昌、安遠軍節度副使，起知光州，以泰寧軍節度副使徙泗州，又徙泰州，卒。

translations.literal: After a long interval he was moved to deputy military commissioners of Wuchang and Anyuan armies, then recalled as prefect of Guang Prefecture; as deputy military commissioner of Taining Army he was moved to Si Prefecture, then again to Tai Prefecture, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was moved to deputy military commissioner of Wuchang and Anyuan armies, then recalled as prefect of Guang Prefecture; as deputy military commissioner of Taining Army he was moved to Si Prefecture, then again to Tai Prefecture, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 子：調，終尚書兵部員外郎、福建路轉運使。

translations.literal: His son Diao ended as yuanwailang in the Bureau of Military Affairs of the Ministry of War and transport commissioner for Fujian Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: His son Diao ended as vice director in the Bureau of Military Affairs of the Ministry of War and transport commissioner for Fujian Circuit.

sentences.zh: 梅詢，字昌言，宣州宣城人。

translations.literal: Mei Xun, courtesy name Changyan, was a man of Xuancheng in Xuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Mei Xun, styled Changyan, was a native of Xuancheng in Xuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少好學，有辭辨。

translations.literal: From youth he loved study and had skill in rhetoric and debate.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved study and was gifted in rhetoric and debate.

sentences.zh: 進士及第，為利豐監判官。

translations.literal: Having passed the jinshi examination, he served as aide at Lifeng Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and served as aide at Lifeng Directorate.

sentences.zh: 後以秘書省著作佐郎、御史臺推勘官，預考進士於崇政殿，真宗過殿廬，奇其占對詳敏，召試中書，除集賢院。

translations.literal: Later, as zuozuo in the Secretariat and an investigating officer of the Censorate, he took part in examining jinshi candidates in the Chongzheng Hall; Emperor Zhenzong passed the hall quarters and was struck by his detailed and nimble responses, summoned him for a test at the Secretariat Chancellery, and appointed him to the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as an associate compiler in the Secretariat and an investigating officer of the Censorate, he took part in examining jinshi candidates in the Chongzheng Hall; Emperor Zhenzong passed the hall quarters and was struck by his detailed and nimble responses, summoned him for a test at the Secretariat Chancellery, and appointed him to the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 李繼遷攻靈州急，吳淑上書請遣使諭秦、隴以西諸戎，使攻繼遷。

translations.literal: When Li Jiqian pressed the attack on Ling Prefecture, Wu Shu memorialized asking that an envoy be sent to instruct the various Rong tribes west of Qin and Long to attack Jiqian.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jiqian pressed the attack on Ling Prefecture, Wu Shu memorialized asking that an envoy be sent to instruct the various Rong tribes west of Qin and Long to attack Jiqian.

sentences.zh: 詢亦請以朔方授潘羅支，使自攻取。

translations.literal: Xun also proposed granting the Shuofang region to Pan Luozhi so that he might attack and capture it himself.
translations.idiomatic: Xun also proposed granting the Shuofang region to Pan Luozhi so that he might attack and capture it himself.

sentences.zh: 帝問誰可使羅支者，詢請行，未至而靈州陷。

translations.literal: The emperor asked who could be sent to Luozhi; Xun volunteered to go, but before he arrived Ling Prefecture fell.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked who could be sent to Luozhi; Xun volunteered to go, but before he arrived Ling Prefecture fell.

sentences.zh: 還，為三司戶部判官。

translations.literal: On his return he served as an aide in the Revenue Section of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he served as an aide in the Revenue Section of the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 詢自以為遇主知，屢上書陳論西北事。

translations.literal: Xun considered himself singled out by his lord and repeatedly submitted memorials discussing northwestern affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Xun considered himself singled out by his lord and repeatedly submitted memorials discussing northwestern affairs.

sentences.zh: 時契丹數侵河北，詢請遣大臣臨邊督戰，募遊手擊賊。

translations.literal: At the time the Khitan repeatedly raided Hebei; Xun asked that a senior minister be sent to the border to supervise campaigning and that vagabonds be recruited to strike the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Khitan repeatedly raided Hebei; Xun asked that a senior minister be sent to the border to supervise campaigning and that vagabonds be recruited to strike the enemy.

sentences.zh: 又論曹瑋、馬知節才可用，傅潛、楊瓊敗當誅，田紹斌、王榮等可責其效以贖過，凡數十事，其言甚壯。

translations.literal: He also argued that Cao Wei and Ma Zhijie had talent that could be used; that Fu Qian and Yang Qiong, having been defeated, deserved execution; and that Tian Shaobin, Wang Rong, and others could be charged to achieve results and redeem their faults—several dozen items in all, stated in very forceful terms.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that Cao Wei and Ma Zhijie had talent that could be used; that Fu Qian and Yang Qiong, having been defeated, deserved execution; and that Tian Shaobin, Wang Rong, and others could be charged to achieve results and redeem their faults—several dozen items in all, stated in very forceful terms.

sentences.zh: 帝欲命知制誥，李沆力言其險薄望輕，不可用。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to appoint him drafter of edicts, but Li Hang forcefully urged that he was dangerous, shallow, and of little standing, and could not be used.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to appoint him drafter of edicts, but Li Hang forcefully urged that he was dangerous, shallow, and of little standing, and could not be used.

sentences.zh: 後斷田訟失實，降通判杭州，知蘇州，就徙兩浙轉運副使，判三司開拆司。

translations.literal: Later, for a false ruling in a land dispute, he was demoted to vice prefect of Hang Prefecture; he became prefect of Suzhou, was thereupon transferred to deputy transport commissioner of the Two Zhe circuits, and judged the Disbursement Office of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for a false ruling in a land dispute, he was demoted to vice prefect of Hang Prefecture; he became prefect of Suzhou, was thereupon transferred to deputy transport commissioner of the Two Zhe circuits, and judged the Disbursement Office of the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 坐議天書，出知濠州。

translations.literal: For discussing the Heavenly Writ he was sent out as prefect of Hao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: For discussing the Heavenly Writ he was sent out as prefect of Hao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 為湖北轉運使，擅假驛馬與邵曄子省親疾而馬死，奪官一級，降通判襄州。

translations.literal: As transport commissioner for Hubei he arbitrarily lent relay horses to Shao Ye's son to visit his sick father; the horses died, and one rank was stripped from him and he was demoted to vice prefect of Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: As transport commissioner for Hubei he arbitrarily lent relay horses to Shao Ye's son to visit his sick father; the horses died, and one rank was stripped from him and he was demoted to vice prefect of Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 知鄂州，徙蘇州，為陝西轉運使。

translations.literal: He served as prefect of E Prefecture, was moved to Suzhou, and became transport commissioner for Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of E Prefecture, was moved to Suzhou, and became transport commissioner for Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 坐薦舉朱能，貶懷州團練副使。

translations.literal: For recommending Zhu Neng he was demoted to deputy military training commissioner of Huai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: For recommending Zhu Neng he was demoted to deputy military training commissioner of Huai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 又以善寇準，徙池州。

translations.literal: Because he had been friendly with Kou Zhun he was moved to Chi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had been friendly with Kou Zhun he was moved to Chi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 起知廣德軍，歷楚、壽、陝州。

translations.literal: He was recalled as prefect of Guangde Army and served in succession at Chu, Shou, and Shaan prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as prefect of Guangde Army and served in succession at Chu, Shou, and Shaan prefectures.

sentences.zh: 復直集賢院，改直昭文館、知荊南，擢龍圖閣待制，糾察在京刑獄。

translations.literal: He was restored to the Hall of Assembled Worthies, changed to the Hall of Illustrious Literature as prefect of Jingnan, was promoted to drafting academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall, and investigated capital criminal cases.
translations.idiomatic: He was restored to the Hall of Assembled Worthies, changed to the Hall of Illustrious Literature as prefect of Jingnan, was promoted to drafting academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall, and investigated capital criminal cases.

sentences.zh: 歷龍圖閣直學士、樞密直學士，知通進銀臺司，判流內銓，為翰林侍讀學士、群牧使。

translations.literal: He served in succession as academician of the Dragon Diagram Pavilion, academician of the Palace Secretariat, commissioner of the Bureau for Transmission of Imperial Orders and the Silver Terrace, judged the Bureau of Inner Circuits, and was Hanlin reader-in-waiting and herds commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as academician of the Dragon Diagram Pavilion, academician of the Palace Secretariat, commissioner of the Bureau for Transmission of Imperial Orders and the Silver Terrace, judged the Bureau of Inner Circuits, and was Hanlin reader-in-waiting and herds commissioner.

sentences.zh: 累遷給事中、知審官院。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to supervisory censor and director of the Bureau for Review of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in succession to supervisory censor and director of the Bureau for Review of Appointments.

sentences.zh: 仁宗御邇英閣，讀《正說養民篇》，覽歷代戶口登耗之數，顧謂侍臣曰：「今天下民籍幾何？

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong, in the Esteemed Classics Hall, read the chapter "Correct Discourse on Nourishing the People" and, scanning the figures for household registers rising and falling through the dynasties, turned to the attendant ministers and said, "How many are registered households in the realm today?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong, in the Esteemed Classics Hall, read the chapter "Correct Discourse on Nourishing the People" and, scanning the figures for household registers rising and falling through the dynasties, turned to the attendant ministers and said, "How many are registered households in the realm today?"

sentences.zh: 」詢對曰：「先帝所作，蓋述前代帝王恭儉有節，則戶口充羨；

translations.literal: Xun replied: "What the late emperor composed essentially sets forth that when emperors of old were reverent, frugal, and restrained, household registers were full and abundant;"
translations.idiomatic: Xun replied: "What the late emperor composed essentially sets forth that when emperors of old were reverent, frugal, and restrained, household registers were full and abundant;"

sentences.zh: 賦斂無藝，則版圖衰減。

translations.literal: when levies were indiscriminate, the register shrank and declined.
translations.idiomatic: when levies were indiscriminate, the register shrank and declined.

sentences.zh: 炳然在目，作鑒後王。

translations.literal: It lies plainly before the eyes, a mirror for later kings.
translations.idiomatic: It lies plainly before the eyes, a mirror for later kings.

sentences.zh: 自五代之季，生齒凋耗，太祖受命，而太宗、真宗休養百姓，天下戶口之數，蓋倍於前矣。

translations.literal: From the end of the Five Dynasties the population withered; once Taizu received the Mandate, Taizong and Zhenzong nourished the people, and household registers in the realm roughly doubled those of before."
translations.idiomatic: From the end of the Five Dynasties the population withered; once Taizu received the Mandate, Taizong and Zhenzong nourished the people, and household registers in the realm roughly doubled those of before."

sentences.zh: 」因詔三司及編修院檢閱以聞。

translations.literal: The emperor therefore ordered the Three Departments and the Compilation Institute to examine and report.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor therefore ordered the Three Departments and the Compilation Institute to examine and report.

sentences.zh: 病足，出知許州，卒。

translations.literal: Ill in the feet, he was sent out as prefect of Xu Prefecture and died.
translations.idiomatic: Ill in the feet, he was sent out as prefect of Xu Prefecture and died.

sentences.zh: 故事，侍讀學士無出外者。

translations.literal: By precedent, Hanlin readers-in-waiting were not posted outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, Hanlin readers-in-waiting were not posted outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 天禧中，張知白罷參知政事，領此職，始出知大名府。

translations.literal: In the Tianxi era, Zhang Zhibai, having left his post as participant in governance, held this office and was the first sent out as prefect of Daming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianxi era, Zhang Zhibai, having left his post as participant in governance, held this office and was the first sent out as prefect of Daming Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 非歷二府而出者自詢始。

translations.literal: Xun was the first to be posted outside without having passed through both administrations.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was the first to be posted outside without having passed through both administrations.

sentences.zh: 詢性卞急好進，而侈於奉養，至老不衰。

translations.literal: Xun's nature was abrupt and impatient for advancement, yet extravagant in his upkeep, which did not diminish even in old age.
translations.idiomatic: Xun's nature was abrupt and impatient for advancement, yet extravagant in his upkeep, which did not diminish even in old age.

sentences.zh: 然數為朝廷言兵。

translations.literal: Yet he spoke on military affairs for the court on many occasions.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he spoke on military affairs for the court on many occasions.

sentences.zh: 在濠州，夢人告曰：「呂丞相至矣。

translations.literal: While at Hao Prefecture he dreamed that someone told him, "Vice Director Lü has arrived."
translations.idiomatic: While at Hao Prefecture he dreamed that someone told him, "Vice Director Lü has arrived."

sentences.zh: 」既而呂夷簡通判州事，故待之甚厚。

translations.literal: Presently Lü Yijian came as vice prefect of the prefecture, and therefore treated him with great kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Presently Lü Yijian came as vice prefect of the prefecture, and therefore treated him with great kindness.

sentences.zh: 其後，援詢於廢斥中，以至貴顯，夷簡力也。

translations.literal: Later, drawing Xun up from disgrace and dismissal to the highest eminence was largely Yijian's doing.
translations.idiomatic: Later, drawing Xun up from disgrace and dismissal to the highest eminence was largely Yijian's doing.

sentences.zh: 馬元方

translations.literal: Ma Yuanfang
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yuanfang

sentences.zh: 馬元方，字景山，濮州鄄城人。

translations.literal: Ma Yuanfang, courtesy name Jingshan, was a man of Yuncheng in Pu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yuanfang, styled Jingshan, was a native of Yuncheng in Pu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父應圖，嘗知頓丘縣，太宗攻幽州，應圖部芻糧，沒虜中。

translations.literal: His father Yingtu had once served as magistrate of Dunqiu County; when Taizong attacked You Prefecture, Yingtu led forage and was lost among the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yingtu had once served as magistrate of Dunqiu County; when Taizong attacked You Prefecture, Yingtu led forage and was lost among the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 元方去髮為浮屠，間行求父屍，不得，訴於朝。

translations.literal: Yuanfang shaved his head and became a monk, traveling secretly to seek his father's corpse; he could not find it and appealed at court.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfang shaved his head and became a monk, traveling secretly to seek his father's corpse; he could not find it and appealed at court.

sentences.zh: 上哀之，為官其兄元吉。

translations.literal: The emperor pitied him and granted office to his elder brother Yuanji.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pitied him and granted office to his elder brother Yuanji.

sentences.zh: 元方，淳化三年進士及第，為韋城縣主簿，改大理寺評事、知萬年縣。

translations.literal: Yuanfang passed the jinshi in the third year of Chunhua and served as recorder of Weicheng County, then was changed to reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review and magistrate of Wannian County.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfang passed the jinshi in the third year of Chunhua and served as recorder of Weicheng County, then was changed to reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review and magistrate of Wannian County.

sentences.zh: 諸將討李繼遷，關輔轉餉逾瀚海，多失亡，獨元方所部全十九。

translations.literal: When the generals campaigned against Li Jiqian, transport across the passes beyond the Hanhai Sea suffered many losses, but only Yuanfang's jurisdiction preserved nineteen parts in twenty.
translations.idiomatic: When the generals campaigned against Li Jiqian, transport across the passes beyond the Hanhai Sea suffered many losses, but only Yuanfang's jurisdiction preserved nineteen parts in twenty.

sentences.zh: 以勞，遷本寺丞，為御史臺推勘官，遷殿中丞。

translations.literal: For this merit he was promoted to vice director in the same court and became an investigating officer of the Censorate, then was promoted to palace director.
translations.idiomatic: For this merit he was promoted to vice director in the same court and became an investigating officer of the Censorate, then was promoted to palace director.

sentences.zh: 戶部使陳恕奏為判官，元方言：「方春民貧，請預貸庫錢，至夏秋，令以絹輸官。

translations.literal: When Ministry of Revenue commissioner Chen Shu submitted him as a judge, Yuanfang said: "It is early spring and the people are poor; I ask that treasury funds be advanced now, and in summer and autumn they be made to deliver silk to the government."
translations.idiomatic: When Ministry of Revenue commissioner Chen Shu submitted him as a judge, Yuanfang said: "It is early spring and the people are poor; I ask that treasury funds be advanced now, and in summer and autumn they be made to deliver silk to the government."

sentences.zh: 」行之，公私果便，因下其法諸路。

translations.literal: This was carried out; public and private interests were indeed convenient, and on that basis his method was promulgated to all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: This was carried out; public and private interests were indeed convenient, and on that basis his method was promulgated to all circuits.

sentences.zh: 知徐州，改太常博士、梓州路轉運使。

translations.literal: He became prefect of Xu Prefecture, then Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and transport commissioner for Zizhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He became prefect of Xu Prefecture, then erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and transport commissioner for Zizhou Circuit.

sentences.zh: 後知鄆州，量括牧地數千頃。

translations.literal: Later he became prefect of Yan Prefecture and surveyed and registered several thousand qing of pasture land.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became prefect of Yan Prefecture and surveyed and registered several thousand qing of pasture land.

sentences.zh: 為京東轉運副使，遷轉運使。

translations.literal: He served as deputy transport commissioner for the Jingdong Circuit and was promoted to transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He served as deputy transport commissioner for the Jingdong Circuit and was promoted to transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 按部至濮州，被酒毆知州蔣信，降知宿州，下詔切責之。

translations.literal: On an inspection tour reaching Pu Prefecture he, while drunk, beat Prefect Jiang Xin and was demoted to prefect of Su Prefecture; an edict sharply rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: On an inspection tour reaching Pu Prefecture he, while drunk, beat Prefect Jiang Xin and was demoted to prefect of Su Prefecture; an edict sharply rebuked him.

sentences.zh: 徙滑州，為京西轉運使，知應天府，累遷太常少卿。

translations.literal: He was moved to Hua Prefecture, became transport commissioner for the Jingxi Circuit, and prefect of Ying Prefecture, rising in succession to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Hua Prefecture, became transport commissioner for the Jingxi Circuit, and prefect of Ying Prefecture, rising in succession to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 擢右諫議大夫、權三司使公事，眾論不以為允。

translations.literal: He was promoted to right remonstrance and drafting commissioner and acting commissioner of the Three Departments; public opinion did not regard this as fitting.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to right remonstrance and drafting commissioner and acting commissioner of the Three Departments; public opinion did not regard this as fitting.

sentences.zh: 真宗謂宰臣曰：「元方在三司，何多謗也？

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong said to the chief ministers: "Why is Yuanfang so much slandered in the Three Departments?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong said to the chief ministers: "Why is Yuanfang so much slandered in the Three Departments?"

sentences.zh: 」王旦曰：「元方盡心營職，然其性卞急，且不納僚屬議，而醜言詆之，所以賈怨。

translations.literal: Wang Dan said: "Yuanfang devotes his heart to duty, yet his nature is abrupt and impatient, he does not accept the counsel of subordinates, and he speaks vilely to defame them—hence he buys resentment."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dan said: "Yuanfang devotes his heart to duty, yet his nature is abrupt and impatient, he does not accept the counsel of subordinates, and he speaks vilely to defame them—hence he buys resentment."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「僚屬顧不有賢俊邪？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Do his subordinates not include able and eminent men?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Do his subordinates not include able and eminent men?"

sentences.zh: 」歲餘，以煩苛罷。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was dismissed for being vexatious in detail.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was dismissed for being vexatious in detail.

sentences.zh: 進給事中、權知開封府。

translations.literal: He was advanced to supervisory censor and acting prefect of Kaifeng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to supervisory censor and acting prefect of Kaifeng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以樞密直學士知幷州，留再任，賜白金五百兩，詔中書諭以委屬之意。

translations.literal: As academician of the Palace Secretariat he became prefect of Bing Prefecture; he was retained for a second term and granted five hundred taels of white silver, with an edict from the Secretariat Chancellery conveying the intent of entrustment.
translations.idiomatic: As academician of the Palace Secretariat he became prefect of Bing Prefecture; he was retained for a second term and granted five hundred taels of white silver, with an edict from the Secretariat Chancellery conveying the intent of entrustment.

sentences.zh: 官至兵部侍郎，卒。

translations.literal: He reached office as vice minister of war and died.
translations.idiomatic: He reached office as vice minister of war and died.

sentences.zh: 薛田，字希稷，河中河東人。

translations.literal: Xue Tian, courtesy name Xiji, was a man of Hedong in Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Tian, styled Xiji, was a native of Hedong in Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 少師事种放，與魏野友善。

translations.literal: In youth he studied under Zhong Fang and was friendly with Wei Ye.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied under Zhong Fang and was friendly with Wei Ye.

sentences.zh: 進士，起家丹州推官。

translations.literal: As a jinshi he began his career as an investigating officer in Dan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: As a jinshi he began his career as an investigating officer in Dan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 李允正知延州，辟為從事，向敏中至，亦薦其材。

translations.literal: When Li Yunzheng became prefect of Yan Prefecture he engaged Tian on his staff; when Xiang Minzhong arrived he too recommended Tian's talent.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Yunzheng became prefect of Yan Prefecture he engaged Tian on his staff; when Xiang Minzhong arrived he too recommended Tian's talent.

sentences.zh: 改著作佐郎、知中江縣。

translations.literal: He was changed to associate compiler and magistrate of Zhongjiang County.
translations.idiomatic: He was changed to associate compiler and magistrate of Zhongjiang County.

sentences.zh: 真宗祀汾陰，田時居父喪，經度制置使陳堯叟奏起通判陝州。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhenzong sacrificed at Fenyin, Tian was then in mourning for his father; the logistics and provisioning commissioner Chen Yaoshou memorialized to recall him as vice prefect of Shan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhenzong sacrificed at Fenyin, Tian was then in mourning for his father; the logistics and provisioning commissioner Chen Yaoshou memorialized to recall him as vice prefect of Shan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 還，拜監察御史，以母憂去。

translations.literal: On his return he was appointed investigating censor and left office on account of his mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed investigating censor and left office on account of his mother's mourning.

sentences.zh: 會祀太清宮，又用丁謂奏，起通判亳州。

translations.literal: At the sacrifice to the Grand Purity Palace, on Ding Wei's memorial he was again recalled as vice prefect of Bo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the sacrifice to the Grand Purity Palace, on Ding Wei's memorial he was again recalled as vice prefect of Bo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 遷殿中侍御史、權三司度支判官，改侍御史、益州路轉運使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to palace attendant censor and acting judge of the Revenue Section of the Three Departments, then attendant censor and transport commissioner for Yizhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to palace attendant censor and acting judge of the Revenue Section of the Three Departments, then attendant censor and transport commissioner for Yizhou Circuit.

sentences.zh: 民間以鐵錢重，私為券以便交易，謂之「交子」，而富家專之，數致爭訟。

translations.literal: Because iron cash was heavy, the people privately made notes to ease exchange, called "jiaozi," which wealthy families monopolized, often leading to lawsuits.
translations.idiomatic: Because iron cash was heavy, the people privately made notes to ease exchange, called "jiaozi," which wealthy families monopolized, often leading to lawsuits.

sentences.zh: 田請置交子務，以榷其出入，未報。

translations.literal: Tian requested establishment of a jiaozi office to tax its issues; there was no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Tian requested establishment of a jiaozi office to tax its issues; there was no reply.

sentences.zh: 及寇瑊守益州，卒奏用其議，蜀人便之。

translations.literal: When Kou Jian held Yiz Prefecture he finally memorialized adoption of the proposal, and the people of Shu found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: When Kou Jian held Yiz Prefecture he finally memorialized adoption of the proposal, and the people of Shu found it convenient.

sentences.zh: 就除陝西轉運使，進直昭文館、知河南府，復入度支為副使。

translations.literal: He was thereupon appointed transport commissioner for Shaanxi, advanced to the Hall of Illustrious Literature as prefect of Henan, and re-entered the Revenue Section as deputy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was thereupon appointed transport commissioner for Shaanxi, advanced to the Hall of Illustrious Literature as prefect of Henan, and re-entered the Revenue Section as deputy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 使契丹還，擢龍圖閣待制、知天雄軍。

translations.literal: On his return from an embassy to the Khitan he was promoted to drafting academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and prefect of Tianxiong Army.
translations.idiomatic: On his return from an embassy to the Khitan he was promoted to drafting academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and prefect of Tianxiong Army.

sentences.zh: 未幾，擢知開封府，以樞密直學士知益州，累遷左司郎中。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to prefect of Kaifeng and, as academician of the Palace Secretariat, prefect of Yizhou, rising in succession to left director in the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to prefect of Kaifeng and, as academician of the Palace Secretariat, prefect of Yizhou, rising in succession to left director in the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 代還，知審刑院。

translations.literal: On his replacement and return he directed the Court for Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: On his replacement and return he directed the Court for Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 羌人內寇，特遷右諫議大夫、知延州。

translations.literal: When the Qiang raided inward he was specially promoted to right remonstrance and prefect of Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qiang raided inward he was specially promoted to right remonstrance and prefect of Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 久之，以疾徙同州，又徙永興軍，辭不行，卒。

translations.literal: After a long interval, because of illness he was moved to Tong Prefecture, then again to Yongxing Army; he declined to go and died.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval, because of illness he was moved to Tong Prefecture, then again to Yongxing Army; he declined to go and died.

sentences.zh: 田性頗和厚，初以幹敏數為大臣所稱，後屢更任使，所治無赫赫名。

translations.literal: Tian's disposition was rather mild and generous; at first his diligence and keenness won praise from senior ministers several times, but after repeated appointments what he governed won no striking reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Tian's disposition was rather mild and generous; at first his diligence and keenness won praise from senior ministers several times, but after repeated appointments what he governed won no striking reputation.

sentences.zh: 寇瑊，字次公，汝州臨汝人。

translations.literal: Kou Jian, courtesy name Cigong, was a man of Linru in Ruzhou Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Jian, styled Cigong, was a native of Linru in Ru Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初，母夢神人授珠，吞之而娠，生而眉目美秀。

translations.literal: At the beginning, his mother dreamed that a divine person gave her a pearl; she swallowed it and became pregnant; when he was born his eyebrows and eyes were beautiful and fine.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, his mother dreamed that a deity handed her a pearl; she swallowed it and conceived, and at birth his features were handsome and refined.

sentences.zh: 擢進士，授蓬州軍事推官。

translations.literal: He was selected as jinshi and appointed military pushing officer of Peng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed military legal officer of Peng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 李順餘黨謝才盛等復起為盜，瑊設方略，擒送京師。

translations.literal: Remnants of Li Shun's faction such as Xie Caisheng again rose as bandits; Jian devised stratagems, captured them, and sent them to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When survivors of Li Shun's faction such as Xie Caisheng again took to banditry, Kou Jian devised a plan, captured them, and sent them to the capital.

sentences.zh: 徙開封推官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to pushing officer of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to legal officer of the Kaifeng Prefecture office.

sentences.zh: 會施州蠻叛，轉運使移瑊權領施州。

translations.literal: It happened that the Man of Shi Prefecture rebelled; the transport commissioner moved Jian to act as head of Shi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yi tribes of Shi Prefecture rebelled, the transport commissioner assigned Kou Jian to govern the prefecture on a provisional basis.

sentences.zh: 先是，戍兵仰他州饋糧，瑊至，請募人入米，償以鹽，軍食遂足，而民力紓。

translations.literal: Before this, garrison troops relied on grain supplied from other prefectures; when Jian arrived, he requested to recruit people to bring in grain and repay them with salt—the military provisions were then sufficient, and the people's labor was relieved.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the garrison had depended on grain shipped in from other prefectures; upon his arrival Kou Jian had people bring in grain in exchange for salt, so the army's food supply was secured while easing the burden on the populace.

sentences.zh: 復招諭高州刺史田彥伊子承寶入朝，得給印紙為高州官族。

translations.literal: He also summoned and persuaded Tian Chengbao, son of Gaozhou Prefect Tian Yanyi, to enter court, obtaining sealed credentials designating him as a Gaozhou official clan.
translations.idiomatic: He also persuaded Tian Chengbao, son of Gaozhou Prefect Tian Yanyi, to come to court, and secured imperial credentials establishing him as an official clan of Gaozhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，溪南蠻復內寇，瑊率眾擒其酋領戮之，以白芀子弟數百人築柵，守其險要。

translations.literal: Before long the Man south of the streams again raided inward; Jian led the troops, captured their chieftain and executed him, and used several hundred Baizhu youth to build stockades guarding strategic passes.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Yi south of the streams raided again; Kou Jian led his forces, captured their chieftain and put him to death, and employed several hundred Baizhu tribesmen to build stockades at key defiles.

sentences.zh: 就除大理寺丞、知開州，遷殿中丞、通判河南府。

translations.literal: He was immediately appointed assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review and prefect of Kai Prefecture, then promoted to director of the Palace Bureau and vice prefect of Henan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was promptly made assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review and magistrate of Kai Prefecture, then promoted to director of the Palace Bureau and vice prefect of Henan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 坐解送諸料失實，降監晉州稅。

translations.literal: For delivering submitted materials with inaccuracies in the facts, he was demoted to supervisor of Jin Prefecture tax.
translations.idiomatic: Because documents he submitted contained false particulars, he was demoted to supervisor of tax collection in Jin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以太常博士通判幷州，改監察御史。

translations.literal: As erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices he served as vice prefect of Bing Prefecture, then was changed to investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices he was vice prefect of Bing Prefecture, then transferred to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 真宗祀汾陰，王嗣宗知永興，辟權通判，專領祠事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhenzong sacrificed at Fenyin, Wang Sizong was prefect of Yongxing; he recruited Jian as acting vice prefect, putting him solely in charge of sacrificial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Zhenzong's sacrifice at Fenyin, Wang Sizong, prefect of Yongxing, brought Kou Jian in as acting vice prefect and put him in sole charge of sacrificial affairs.

sentences.zh: 遷殿中侍御史，為開封府判官。

translations.literal: He was promoted to palace attendant censor and made judge of the Kaifeng Prefecture office.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to palace attendant censor and served as judge of the Kaifeng Prefecture office.

sentences.zh: 嘗奏事，帝詢施州備禦之術，因諭之曰：「東川控蠻夷，爾功已試，其為朕鎮撫之。

translations.literal: Once when memorializing, the emperor asked about defensive methods for Shi Prefecture; he therefore instructed him, saying: "East Chuan controls the Man and Yi; your merit has already been tested—go and pacify them for me."
translations.idiomatic: When he once reported to the throne, the emperor inquired about defenses at Shi Prefecture and told him: "East Chuan holds the frontier against the Yi; you have already proved yourself there—pacify the region for me."

sentences.zh: 」命為梓州路轉運使。

translations.literal: He was ordered to be transport commissioner of the Zizhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed transport commissioner of the Zizhou Circuit.

sentences.zh: 晏州多剛縣酋鬥望劫瀘州，燒淯井監，殺官吏。

translations.literal: In Yan Prefecture the chieftain Dou Wang of Gang County repeatedly raided Luzhou, burned Yujing Supervisory Office, and killed officials.
translations.idiomatic: In Yan Prefecture, Dou Wang, chieftain of Gang County, repeatedly raided Luzhou, burned the Yujing Supervisory Office, and murdered officials.

sentences.zh: 瑊趨富順監，命部兵多張旗幟，逾山西北趨戎州，盡取公私舟載糧甲，具音樂，合兩路兵至江安，誘納溪、藍、順史個鬆，南廣移、悅等州刺史及八姓烏蠻首領，使斷賊徑。

translations.literal: Jian hastened to Fushun Supervisory Office, ordered his troops to display many banners and flags, crossed the mountain northwest toward Rong Prefecture, took all public and private boats to transport grain and armor, brought musicians, combined the forces of two circuits at Jiang'an, and induced the Naxi, Lan, Shunshi Gesong, and Nanguang Yi prefects of Yi and Yue, plus the chieftains of the eight Baishi tribes, to cut the bandits' routes.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Jian rushed to Fushun Supervisory Office, had his men raise many banners, crossed the mountains northwest toward Rong Prefecture, commandeered every available boat to carry grain and arms, brought musicians along, mustered the troops of two circuits at Jiang'an, and won over the Naxi, Lan, Shunshi Gesong, and Nanguang Yi prefects of Yi and Yue plus eight Baishi chieftains to block the rebels' paths.

sentences.zh: 用夷法，植竹為誓門，橫竹繫貓、犬、雞各一於其上，老夷人執刀劍，謂之「打誓」，呼曰：「誓與漢家同心擊賊。

translations.literal: Using the Yi method, they planted bamboo to form an oath gate, tied one each of cat, dog, and chicken horizontally on it; old Yi men holding swords and blades called it "da shi," and shouted: "We swear to join hearts with the Han house in striking the bandits."
translations.idiomatic: Following Yi custom they erected a bamboo oath-gate with a cat, dog, and chicken bound across it; aged Yi warriors bearing swords and blades performed what they called "striking the oath," crying: "We swear to stand with the Han in crushing these rebels."

sentences.zh: 」即刺牲血和酒而飲。

translations.literal: They then pierced the sacrificial victim, mixed the blood with wine, and drank it.
translations.idiomatic: Then they pierced the victims, mixed the blood with wine, and drank.

sentences.zh: 瑊給鹽及酒食、針梳、衣服等，付以大榜，約大軍至，揭榜以別逆順，「不殺汝老少，不燒汝欄柵。

translations.literal: Jian gave them salt, wine, food, needles, combs, clothing, and the like, and handed them a large placard, stipulating that when the main army arrived they would post the placard to distinguish loyal from rebellious: "We will not kill your old and young, nor burn your palisades."
translations.idiomatic: Kou Jian supplied salt, wine, provisions, needles, combs, and clothing, and gave them a large proclamation promising that when the main force arrived they would display it to separate the loyal from the rebellious: "We will not slay your women, children, and elderly, nor burn your stockades."

sentences.zh: 」夷人大喜。

translations.literal: The Yi people greatly rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: The Yi were overjoyed.

sentences.zh: 帝遣內殿崇班王懷信議攻討招輯之宜，瑊奏：「夷人嘗於二年春燒淯井監，殺吏民。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Inner Hall Direct Attendant Wang Huaixin to deliberate on the proper course of attack, pacification, and gathering; Jian memorialized: "The Yi once in the second year spring burned Yujing Supervisory Office and killed officials and people."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched Inner Hall Direct Attendant Wang Huaixin to advise on attack and pacification; Kou Jian wrote: "These Yi burned Yujing Supervisory Office and slaughtered officials and civilians in the spring of the second year."

sentences.zh: 既赦貸其罪，復來寇邊，聲言朝廷且招安，得酒食衣服矣。

translations.literal: Although their crimes had been pardoned, they again came raiding the border, loudly proclaiming that the court was about to offer pacification and that they would receive wine, food, and clothing.
translations.idiomatic: Though previously pardoned, they had returned to raid the frontier, boasting that the court would soon offer amnesty and more wine, food, and clothing.

sentences.zh: 若不討除，則戎、瀘、資、榮、富順監諸夷競起為邊害矣。

translations.literal: If they are not punished and eliminated, then the Yi of Rong, Lu, Zi, Rong, and Fushun Supervisory Office will all rise in competition as border harms.
translations.idiomatic: Unless they were crushed, the Yi of Rong, Lu, Zi, Rong, and Fushun Supervisory Office would take it as a signal to harry the borders one after another.

sentences.zh: 」詔發陝西兵，益以白芀子弟合六千三百人，緣淯井溪轉鬥，凡十一陣，破之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Shaanxi troops augmented with Baizhu youth totaling six thousand three hundred; they fought turning along Yujing Stream through eleven formations and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial order Shaanxi troops were reinforced with six thousand three hundred Baizhu tribesmen; fighting along the Yujing Stream through eleven engagements, they broke the enemy.

sentences.zh: 夷人相率來附，納牛羊、銅鼓、器械甚眾，而鬥望猶旅拒不從。

translations.literal: Yi people came in groups to submit, offering cattle, sheep, bronze drums, and weapons in great numbers, while Dou Wang still camped together and refused to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Yi submitted in large numbers, bringing cattle, sheep, bronze drums, and arms in abundance, but Dou Wang continued to hold out with his band.

sentences.zh: 瑊命懷信分兵拔其柵，與都巡檢使符承順進戰思晏江口，鬥望等始驚遽，勢稍卻，明日，復分三道來拒王師，懷信等格戰，瑊乘其後，大破之。

translations.literal: Jian ordered Huaixin to divide troops and capture their stockade; together with Frontier Inspection Commissioner Fu Shunshun he advanced to battle at the mouth of the Siyan River; Dou Wang and the others were first startled and flustered, their momentum slightly retreating; the next day they again came in three divisions to resist the imperial army; Huaixin and others locked in battle; Jian struck from the rear and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Jian had Huaixin split his forces to storm their fort; with Frontier Inspection Commissioner Fu Shunshun he fought at the mouth of the Siyan River, and Dou Wang's men, suddenly unnerved, gave ground; the next day they returned in three columns to oppose the imperial army, but as Huaixin engaged them Kou Jian hit their rear and routed them completely.

sentences.zh: 鬥望眾萬餘，囂不能軍，溺死者眾，遂降。

translations.literal: Dou Wang's force of over ten thousand, in uproar unable to form ranks, many drowned, and they then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Wang's army of more than ten thousand, thrown into chaos and unable to hold formation, lost many men to drowning and at last surrendered.

sentences.zh: 因籍軍之勇悍千人，分五都以隸禁軍，為寧遠指揮，使守淯井監，更建砦柵，浚三壕以環之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he registered a thousand brave and fierce soldiers from the army, divided them into five companies to be attached to the forbidden army as the Ningyuan Command, stationed them to guard Yujing Supervisory Office, rebuilt fortifications and stockades, and dug three moats to encircle it.
translations.idiomatic: He then selected a thousand of the fiercest warriors, organized them into five companies under the forbidden army as the Ningyuan Command to guard Yujing Supervisory Office, rebuilt fortresses and palisades, and dug three encircling moats.

sentences.zh: 就加侍御史，召為三司鹽鐵判官，逾月，出為河北轉運使。

translations.literal: He was immediately additionally appointed attendant censor, summoned as salt and iron judge of the Three Departments, and a month later sent out as transport commissioner of Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: He was promptly promoted to attendant censor, recalled as salt and iron judge of the Three Departments, and a month later dispatched as Hebei transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 天禧中，河決澶淵。

translations.literal: In the Tianxi era the Yellow River burst its banks at Chanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianxi reign the Yellow River broke through at Chanyuan.

sentences.zh: 瑊視役河上，堤墊數里，眾皆奔潰，而瑊獨留自若。

translations.literal: Jian inspected the work on the river; several li of dike collapsed, everyone fled in rout, but Jian alone remained as calm as ever.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Jian oversaw the river works; when several li of embankment gave way the workmen scattered, but he alone stayed calm.

sentences.zh: 須臾，水為折去，眾頗異之。

translations.literal: In a moment the water was turned aside; the crowd greatly marveled at it.
translations.idiomatic: Moments later the current shifted away from them, and onlookers were astonished.

sentences.zh: 遷工部郎中，上言：「契丹約和以來，河北減戍卒之半，而復刺土兵，其實益三分之一，而塞下軍儲不給。

translations.literal: Promoted to director in the Ministry of Works, he submitted: "Since the Khitan peace treaty, Hebei has halved its garrison troops while also conscripting local militia—the actual increase is one third, yet frontier military stores are insufficient."
translations.idiomatic: As director in the Ministry of Works he argued: "Since peace with the Khitan, Hebei has cut garrison strength by half yet raised local militia, increasing numbers by a third in effect while frontier granaries still run short."

sentences.zh: 請行入中、鑿頭、便糴三說之法。

translations.literal: He requested implementing the three methods of enter-to-middle, shaved-head, and convenient-procurement.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed adopting the enter-to-middle, shaved-head, and convenient-procurement grain schemes.

sentences.zh: 」入為三司度支副使。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as vice commissioner of fiscal affairs in the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital as vice commissioner of fiscal affairs in the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以右諫議大夫、集賢院學士知益州。

translations.literal: Before long, as right remonstrance grand master and academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, he was made prefect of Yi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed right remonstrance grand master and academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies and sent out as prefect of Yi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，遷給事中。

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong took the throne, he was promoted to chief of the bureau of memorials.
translations.idiomatic: At Renzong's accession he was promoted to chief of the memorials bureau.

sentences.zh: 瑊與丁謂厚善，帝謂輔臣曰：「瑊有吏幹，毋深譴也。

translations.literal: Jian was on close terms with Ding Wei; the emperor told the chief ministers: "Jian has administrative skill—do not punish him severely."
translations.idiomatic: Kou Jian was close to Ding Wei; the emperor told his chief ministers: "Kou Jian is a capable administrator—do not punish him too harshly."

sentences.zh: 」徙鄧州，坐失舉，降少府監、知金州，復右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Deng Prefecture; for failing in his recommendation duties he was demoted to director of the Palace Maintenance Office and made prefect of Jin Prefecture, then restored to right remonstrance grand master.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Deng Prefecture; after a faulty recommendation he was reduced to director of the Palace Maintenance Office and magistrate of Jin Prefecture, then restored to right remonstrance grand master.

sentences.zh: 會河決，徙知滑州，總領修河。

translations.literal: It happened that the river broke its banks; he was transferred to be prefect of Hua Prefecture and given overall charge of river repair.
translations.idiomatic: When the river breached again he was reassigned to Hua Prefecture and put in overall charge of dyke works.

sentences.zh: 既而以歲饑罷役，瑊言：「病民者特楗芻耳，幸調率已集，若積之經年，則朽腐為棄物，後復興工斂之，是重困也。

translations.literal: Subsequently because of famine the work was halted; Jian said: "What harms the people is only the driven grass and fodder; fortunately the levied deliveries are already gathered—if stored for a full year they will rot and become waste; later when the work is revived and collected again, this would double the distress."
translations.idiomatic: Work was suspended for famine, but Kou Jian warned: "The burden on the people is chiefly the requisitioned fodder; the levies are already in hand—if left a full year they will rot worthless, and collecting them again when work resumes would only deepen their hardship."

sentences.zh: 」乃再詔塞河。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict again ordered the river blocked.
translations.idiomatic: The court then ordered the river sealed again.

sentences.zh: 河平，擢樞密直學士。

translations.literal: When the river was level, he was promoted to académician-direct of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After the river was brought under control he was made académician-direct of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 明年，復給事中、知秦州，又坐失舉奪一官。

translations.literal: The next year he again became chief of memorials and prefect of Qin Prefecture, and again lost one rank for failing in recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he returned as chief of memorials and prefect of Qin Prefecture, only to forfeit one rank again over a bad recommendation.

sentences.zh: 召權三司使，復其官如故。

translations.literal: He was summoned to act as commissioner of the Three Departments and had his former rank restored.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to serve as acting commissioner of the Three Departments, he had his previous rank restored.

sentences.zh: 時有議茶法者，帝訪以利害，瑊曰：「議者未知其要爾。

translations.literal: At the time there were those debating the tea law; the emperor asked him about benefit and harm; Jian said: "The debaters simply do not know its essentials."
translations.idiomatic: When policy on the tea monopoly came under debate, the emperor asked his view; Kou Jian replied: "Those arguing the point do not grasp what matters."

sentences.zh: 河北入中兵食，皆仰給於商旅。

translations.literal: Hebei enter-to-middle military provisions all depend on supply from traveling merchants.
translations.idiomatic: Hebei's enter-to-middle grain for the army relies entirely on merchant convoys.

sentences.zh: 若官盡其利，則商旅不行，而邊民困於饋運，茶法豈可以數更？

translations.literal: If the state monopolizes every profit, then traveling merchants will not go, and frontier people will be distressed by transport levies—how can the tea law be changed repeatedly?
translations.idiomatic: If the government takes every profit for itself, merchants will stop coming and frontier folk will buckle under transport duties—why keep rewriting the tea law?

sentences.zh: 」帝然之。

translations.literal: The emperor considered this correct.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 權知開封府，戚里有毆妻至死，更赦事發者。

translations.literal: Acting as prefect of Kaifeng, a consort clansman beat his wife to death—a case that came to light after an amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: While acting prefect of Kaifeng, a consort clansman was found to have beaten his wife to death after an amnesty had already covered the offense.

sentences.zh: 太后怒曰：「夫婦齊體，奈何毆致死邪？

translations.literal: The empress dowager angrily said: "Husband and wife are one body—how can one beat her to death?"
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager fumed: "Husband and wife share one body—how could he beat her to death?"

sentences.zh: 」瑊對曰：「傷居限外，事在赦前，有司不敢亂天下法。

translations.literal: Jian replied: "The injury fell outside the statutory limit; the matter occurred before the amnesty—the officials dare not disturb the law of the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Kou Jian answered: "The wounds fell outside the statutory limit and the act preceded the amnesty; the court cannot overturn the law of the land."

sentences.zh: 」卒免死。

translations.literal: In the end he was exempted from death.
translations.idiomatic: The man was spared execution in the end.

sentences.zh: 天聖末，再使契丹，未行而卒。

translations.literal: At the end of Tiansheng he was again sent as envoy to the Khitan; before departing he died.
translations.idiomatic: Near the close of the Tiansheng era he was again dispatched as envoy to the Khitan but died before he could set out.

sentences.zh: 瑊少孤，鞠於祖母王氏，及登朝，以妻封邑回授之，朝臣得回封祖母自瑊始。

translations.literal: Jian was orphaned young and raised by his grandmother Lady Wang; after entering court he used his wife's enfeoffment to confer back upon her—the first courtier to obtain retroactive enfeoffment for a grandmother began with Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Jian lost his father young and was raised by his grandmother Lady Wang; once in office he redirected his wife's fief back to her—the first courtier to win a grandmother's enfeoffment by such transfer was Kou Jian.

sentences.zh: 性頗疏財，通音律，知術數。

translations.literal: By nature he was rather openhanded with money, versed in music, and knowledgeable in divination and numerology.
translations.idiomatic: He was generous with money by nature, understood music, and practiced divination.

sentences.zh: 初附丁謂，故少達，及謂敗左遷，鬱鬱不自得，秘書丞彭齊賦《喪家狗》以刺之。

translations.literal: At first he attached himself to Ding Wei and therefore rose early; after Wei's fall he was demoted and leftward transferred, depressed and ill at ease; Secretariat director Peng Qi composed "The Bereaved Dog" to satirize him.
translations.idiomatic: Early on he rode Ding Wei's coattails and rose quickly; when Ding Wei fell he was demoted and sank into brooding; Secretariat Director Peng Qi lampooned him in "The Bereaved Dog."

sentences.zh: 楊日嚴

translations.literal: Yang Riyan
translations.idiomatic: Yang Riyan

sentences.zh: 楊日嚴，字垂訓，河南人。

translations.literal: Yang Riyan, courtesy name Chuixun, was a man of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Riyan, styled Chuixun, was a native of Henan.

sentences.zh: 進士及第，試秘書省校書郎、知安丘縣。

translations.literal: Having passed the jinshi examination, he was tried as collator of the Secretariat and made prefect of Anqiu County.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and served as collator in the Secretariat before becoming magistrate of Anqiu County.

sentences.zh: 三司辟為檢法官，遷大理寺丞，又為本寺檢法官，監都進奏院，通判亳、陳二州，判吏部南曹兼登聞鼓院。

translations.literal: The Three Departments recruited him as legal examiner; he was promoted to assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review, again served as legal examiner of that court, supervised the Directorate of Memorials, served as vice prefect of Bo and Chen Prefectures, and judged the Southern Bureau of the Ministry of Personnel while also holding the Petition Drum Court.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Departments brought him in as legal examiner; he rose to assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review, served again as that court's examiner, supervised the Directorate of Memorials, was vice prefect of Bo and Chen Prefectures, and judged the Ministry of Personnel's Southern Bureau while also overseeing the Petition Drum Court.

sentences.zh: 出知襄州，徙廬、鄲二州，入為開封府判官。

translations.literal: He went out as prefect of Xiang Prefecture, was transferred to Lu and Yun Prefectures, and entered the capital as judge of the Kaifeng Prefecture office.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Xiang Prefecture, then transferred to Lu and Yun Prefectures before returning to the capital as judge of the Kaifeng Prefecture office.

sentences.zh: 使契丹還，為兩浙轉運副使。

translations.literal: Returning from an embassy to the Khitan, he became vice transport commissioner of the Two Zhe Circuits.
translations.idiomatic: After returning from an embassy to the Khitan, he was appointed vice transport commissioner of the Two Zhe Circuits.

sentences.zh: 未行，會青、徐饑，改京東轉運使。

translations.literal: Before departing, it happened that Qing and Xu suffered famine; he was changed to transport commissioner of the Eastern Capital Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the post, famine struck Qing and Xu, and he was reassigned as transport commissioner of the Eastern Capital Circuit.

sentences.zh: 因請江、淮、陝西轉粟五十萬，以賑貧民；

translations.literal: Thereupon he requested transporting five hundred thousand bushels of grain from the Jiang, Huai, and Shaanxi regions to relieve the poor people.
translations.idiomatic: He then requested that five hundred thousand bushels of grain be shipped from the Jiang, Huai, and Shaanxi regions to feed the destitute.

sentences.zh: 又開清河八十里抵暖水河，並堤起倉廩，以便漕運。

translations.literal: He also opened the Qing River for eighty li to reach Nuanshui River, and built granaries along the dike to facilitate canal transport.
translations.idiomatic: He also dredged the Qing River for eighty li to link it with the Nuanshui River and built granaries along the embankment to ease grain transport.

sentences.zh: 加直史館，徙益州轉運使，又徙江淮制置發運使。

translations.literal: He was additionally appointed compiler of the Historiography Institute, transferred to transport commissioner of Yi Prefecture, and again transferred to commissioner for provisioning and dispatch on the Jiang and Huai.
translations.idiomatic: He was made compiler of the Historiography Institute, then moved to transport commissioner of Yi Prefecture and later to commissioner for provisioning and dispatch on the Jiang and Huai.

sentences.zh: 還，歷三司戶部、度支、鹽鐵副使。

translations.literal: Returning, he successively served as vice commissioner of the revenue, fiscal affairs, and salt and iron bureaus in the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: Back at court he served in turn as vice commissioner of the revenue, fiscal affairs, and salt and iron bureaus in the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 累遷太常少卿，以右諫議大夫、集賢院學士知河中府，加樞密直學士、知益州。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; as right remonstrance grand master and academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies he governed Hezhong Prefecture; he was additionally made academician in the Palace Secretariat and prefect of Yi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, served as right remonstrance grand master and academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies at Hezhong Prefecture, and was further appointed academician in the Palace Secretariat and sent out as prefect of Yi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時用兵伐元昊，三司急財用，有詔析戶版為十等，第賦役；

translations.literal: At the time troops were deployed to attack Yuan Hao; the Three Departments urgently needed funds; an edict ordered household registers divided into ten grades to rank tax and corvée.
translations.idiomatic: While the court was campaigning against Yuan Hao, the Three Departments faced a fiscal crunch; an edict split household registers into ten grades to tier taxes and corvée.

sentences.zh: 民以歲租占佃官田廬者，高其估，募輸錢就市為己業，人苦其擾。

translations.literal: For people who occupied official fields and dwellings by annual rent, the valuation was raised and they were recruited to pay money and buy them on the market as private property—the people suffered from the harassment.
translations.idiomatic: Tenants on official fields and dwellings were hit with inflated valuations and pressed to buy the land outright at market rates, to the people's great distress.

sentences.zh: 又陝西奏收市益、梓、利路溪洞馬，而不知其實無馬也，日嚴皆奏罷之。

translations.literal: Also Shaanxi memorialized to purchase horses from the stream-cave routes of the Yi, Zi, and Li circuits without knowing that in fact there were no horses; Riyan memorialized to abolish all of these.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi also proposed buying horses from the stream valleys of the Yi, Zi, and Li circuits without realizing there were scarcely any to buy; Riyan memorialized to have every such measure withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 遷勾當三班院、知通進銀臺司。

translations.literal: He was promoted to administrator of the Three-Rank Court and director of the Directorate for Transmission and the Silver Terrace Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was made administrator of the Three-Rank Court and director of the Directorate for Transmission and the Silver Terrace Office.

sentences.zh: 聞後為守者，其政不便蜀人，因進對，猶從容言：「遠方所宜撫安之，無容變法以生事。

translations.literal: Hearing that his successors as prefects had policies inconvenient to the people of Shu, when he entered audience he still spoke at ease: "Distant regions should be pacified and settled—one must not change laws to create trouble."
translations.idiomatic: Learning that his successors in office had policies that vexed the people of Shu, he still told the throne in measured tones: "Frontier regions need steady reassurance, not new laws that stir up trouble."

sentences.zh: 」遷給事中，以龍圖閣學士知澶州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to chief of the bureau of memorials and, as academician of the Hall of Dragon Diagrams, made prefect of Chan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to chief of the memorials bureau and, as academician of the Hall of Dragon Diagrams, sent out as prefect of Chan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 召權知開封府，吏械囚不謹，囚自殺，坐是罷府事。

translations.literal: He was summoned to act as prefect of Kaifeng; an official shackled a prisoner carelessly and the prisoner killed himself—for this he was removed from prefectural duties.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to act as prefect of Kaifeng, he lost the post when a clerk shackled a prisoner so carelessly that the man killed himself.

sentences.zh: 判太常、司農寺，同知審官院，卒。

translations.literal: He judged the Courts of Imperial Sacrifices and State Granaries, served concurrently as vice director of the Bureau of Appointments, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He served as judge of the Courts of Imperial Sacrifices and State Granaries and as vice director of the Bureau of Appointments, then died.

sentences.zh: 日嚴初為益州轉運使，無他治能，及知益州，頗為蜀人所信愛。

translations.literal: At first as transport commissioner of Yi Prefecture Riyan had no other governing ability, but when he became prefect of Yi Prefecture he was rather trusted and loved by the people of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: As transport commissioner of Yi Prefecture he had shown little administrative talent, yet once he governed the prefecture itself the people of Shu came to trust and esteem him.

sentences.zh: 兄：日華，歷官至太常少卿、三司副使。

translations.literal: Elder brother: Rihua, who rose through offices to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and vice commissioner of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Rihua rose through the ranks to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and vice commissioner of the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 李行簡

translations.literal: Li Xingjian
translations.idiomatic: Li Xingjian

sentences.zh: 李行簡，字易從，同州馮翊人。

translations.literal: Li Xingjian, courtesy name Yicong, was a man of Fengyi in Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xingjian, styled Yicong, was a native of Fengyi in Tong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 家貧，刻志於學，讀《六經》每至夜分，寒暑不易。

translations.literal: His family was poor; he carved his will into study, reading the "Six Classics" each night until midnight, unchanged in cold and heat.
translations.idiomatic: Born poor, he devoted himself utterly to learning, poring over the "Six Classics" each night until midnight through every season without fail.

sentences.zh: 又聚木葉學書，筆法遒勁。

translations.literal: He also gathered tree leaves to practice writing; his brush method was forceful and vigorous.
translations.idiomatic: He even practiced calligraphy on gathered leaves, developing a bold and vigorous hand.

sentences.zh: 與里中富人楊士元同學，既而同時中進士第，士元資遺行簡，謝不取。

translations.literal: He studied together with the wealthy man of the village Yang Shiyuan; afterward they both passed the jinshi examination at the same time; Shiyuan offered funds to Xingjian, who declined to accept.
translations.idiomatic: He studied alongside the local magnate Yang Shiyuan, and when they passed the jinshi examination together Shiyuan offered him money, which he politely refused.

sentences.zh: 起家隴州司理參軍，徙彭州軍事推官。

translations.literal: He began his career as judicial administrator of Long Prefecture, then was transferred to military pushing officer of Peng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He began as judicial administrator of Long Prefecture and was later transferred to military legal officer of Peng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 陵州富民陳子美父死，繼母詐為父書逐出之，累訴不得直，轉運使檄行簡劾正其獄。

translations.literal: In Ling Prefecture the wealthy man Chen Zimei's father died; his stepmother forged his father's writing to drive him out; he repeatedly appealed without obtaining justice; the transport commissioner ordered Xingjian by dispatch to investigate and rectify the case.
translations.idiomatic: In Ling Prefecture, after the wealthy Chen Zimei's father died his stepmother forged a document in the father's hand to expel him; though he appealed repeatedly he could get no redress until the transport commissioner ordered Xingjian to investigate and set the case right.

sentences.zh: 改秘書省著作郎，再遷太常博士、知坊州。

translations.literal: He was changed to compiler in the Secretariat, and again promoted to erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and prefect of Fang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was made compiler in the Secretariat, then promoted to erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and magistrate of Fang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞王嗣宗薦為監察御史，王旦數稱其才，真宗雅亦知之，再遷侍御史。

translations.literal: Censor-in-chief Wang Sizong recommended him as investigating censor; Wang Dan repeatedly praised his talent; Emperor Zhenzong also knew him well, and he was again promoted to attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Wang Sizong recommended him as investigating censor; Wang Dan often praised his ability, and Emperor Zhenzong already held him in regard; he was soon promoted to attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 陝西旱蝗，命往安撫，發倉粟救乏絕，又蠲耀州積年逋租。

translations.literal: Shaanxi suffered drought and locusts; he was ordered to go and pacify the region, opened granary grain to rescue those in want, and also remitted Yao Prefecture's accumulated years of overdue rent.
translations.idiomatic: When drought and locusts struck Shaanxi he was sent to relieve the region, opened granaries to feed the destitute, and remitted years of overdue rent in Yao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 還，擢龍圖閣待制，歷尚書刑部郎中。

translations.literal: Returning, he was promoted to drafting official of the Hall of Dragon Diagrams and successively served as director in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made drafting official of the Hall of Dragon Diagrams and later served as director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 帝數幸龍圖閣，命講《周易》，間訪大臣能否，行簡所對無怨昵，各道其所長，人以為長者。

translations.literal: The emperor several times visited the Hall of Dragon Diagrams and ordered lectures on the "Book of Changes"; he occasionally asked the great ministers about ability; Xingjian's answers held no resentment or partiality—each he spoke of according to his strengths—and people considered him an elder of virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often visited the Hall of Dragon Diagrams for lectures on the "Book of Changes" and would ask his ministers about one another's merits; Xingjian answered without rancor or favoritism, naming each man's strengths, and people regarded him as a man of mature judgment.

sentences.zh: 久之，拜右諫議大夫、集賢院學士。

translations.literal: After a long time he was appointed right remonstrance grand master and academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: In time he was appointed right remonstrance grand master and academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 乾興初，改給事中，以足疾請外，得知河中府，徙虢州，卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianxing he was changed to chief of the bureau of memorials; because of foot ailment he requested an outside post, became prefect of Hezhong Prefecture, was transferred to Guo Prefecture, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianxing era he became chief of the memorials bureau; citing a foot ailment he sought a provincial post, governed Hezhong Prefecture, was transferred to Guo Prefecture, and died.

sentences.zh: 章頻，字簡之，建州浦城人。

translations.literal: Zhang Pin, courtesy name Jianzhi, was a man of Pucheng in Jian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Pin, styled Jianzhi, was a native of Pucheng in Jian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 與弟頔皆以進士試禮部預選，會詔兄弟毋並舉，頻即推其弟，棄去。

translations.literal: He and his younger brother Di both entered the Ministry of Rites jinshi preliminary selection; it happened that an edict forbade brothers from competing together—Pin immediately yielded to his younger brother and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He and his younger brother Di both reached the Ministry of Rites jinshi preselection when an edict barred brothers from competing together; Pin at once stood aside for his brother and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 後六年，乃擢第。

translations.literal: Six years later he finally passed the examination.
translations.idiomatic: Six years later he at last passed the examination.

sentences.zh: 自試秘書省校書郎、知南昌縣，改大理寺丞、知九隴縣，遷殿中丞。

translations.literal: Beginning with trial as collator of the Secretariat and prefect of Nanchang County, he was changed to assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review and prefect of Jiulong County, then promoted to director of the Palace Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He began as collator in the Secretariat and magistrate of Nanchang County, then became assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review and magistrate of Jiulong County before rising to director of the Palace Bureau.

sentences.zh: 眉州大姓孫延世偽為券奪族人田，久不能辨，轉運使使按治之。

translations.literal: In Mei Prefecture the great clan member Sun Yanshi forged a deed to seize a kinsman's fields; for a long time it could not be distinguished; the transport commissioner sent him to investigate and settle the matter.
translations.idiomatic: In Mei Prefecture, Sun Yanshi of a powerful clan forged a deed to seize a relative's land; the case had long gone unresolved until the transport commissioner dispatched him to investigate and adjudicate it.

sentences.zh: 頻視券墨浮朱上，曰：「是必先盜印然後書。

translations.literal: Pin, viewing the ink on the deed, said: "This must have been stamped first and then written."
translations.idiomatic: Examining the deed, Pin saw the ink floating above the vermilion seal and said, "The seal was surely stolen first and only then was the text written."

sentences.zh: 」既引伏，獄未上，而其家人復訴於轉運使，更命知華陽縣黃夢松覆按，無所異。

translations.literal: After he confessed, before the case was submitted his family again sued to the transport commissioner; Huang Mengsong, magistrate of Huayang, was ordered to reinvestigate and found no discrepancy.
translations.idiomatic: He had already confessed, but before the dossier went up his kin appealed again to the transport commissioner; Huang Mengsong of Huayang was sent to review the case and reached the same conclusion.

sentences.zh: 夢松用此入為監察御史，頻坐不時具獄，降監慶州酒，徙知長洲縣。

translations.literal: Mengsong entered the capital as investigating censor on this basis; Pin was demoted for not completing the case on time to supervise Qingzhou wine, then moved to magistrate of Changzhou County.
translations.idiomatic: Mengsong won promotion to investigating censor on that basis, while Pin—faulted for not finishing the dossier on schedule—was demoted to supervise Qingzhou wine and later made magistrate of Changzhou County.

sentences.zh: 天禧初，增置諫官、御史十二人，頻以選得召對，稱旨，擢監察御史。

translations.literal: In the early Tianxi era twelve remonstrance officials and censors were added; Pin was selected, summoned for audience, found pleasing, and promoted to investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianxi began and twelve new remonstrance posts and censorates were created, Pin was chosen, called to audience, pleased the throne, and was raised to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 陳、亳間民訛言兵起，老幼皆奔，命安撫京西。

translations.literal: Between Chen and Bo prefectures the people spread false rumors of armed uprising and old and young all fled; he was ordered to pacify the Western Capital circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors of war ran between Chen and Bo, driving young and old into flight; he was ordered to pacify the Western Capital circuit.

sentences.zh: 還，為三司度支判官。

translations.literal: On his return he served as judge of the Revenue Section of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: Back at court he judged cases in the Revenue Section of the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 青州麻士瑤殺從子溫裕，並其財，遣往按治，士瑤伏誅。

translations.literal: In Qingzhou Ma Shiyao killed his nephew Wen Yu and seized his property; Pin was sent to investigate and Shiyao was executed.
translations.idiomatic: At Qingzhou, Ma Shiyao murdered his nephew Wen Yu and took his estate; Pin was dispatched to investigate, and Shiyao was put to death.

sentences.zh: 又詔鞫邛州牙校訟鹽井事。

translations.literal: He was also ordered to try the case of Ya school officers suing over salt wells in Qiong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was further ordered to hear the suit of Qiong Prefecture military clerks over salt-well rights.

sentences.zh: 皇城使劉美依倚后家受賕，使人市其獄，頻請捕繫，真宗以后故不問。

translations.literal: The Imperial City commissioner Liu Mei, relying on the empress's kin, accepted bribes and had men buy off the case; Pin repeatedly requested arrest and imprisonment, but because of the empress Emperor Zhenzong did not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial City commissioner Liu Mei, backed by the empress's family, took bribes and arranged to buy the case off; Pin repeatedly asked that he be seized, but the emperor, for the empress's sake, would not pursue it.

sentences.zh: 忤旨，出知宣州，改殿中侍御史，遷侍御史。
